53	def _parse(argv):
54	    state = None
55	    rest = []
56	    i = 0
57	    while i < len(argv):
58	        arg = argv[i]
59	        if arg == "--state":
60	            if i + 1 >= len(argv):
61	                _usage()
62	            state = argv[i + 1]
63	            i += 2
64	        elif arg.startswith("--state="):
65	            state = arg[len("--state="):]
66	            i += 1
67	        else:
68	            rest.append(arg)
69	            i += 1
70	    if not state or len(rest) == 0:
71	        _usage()
72	    command, operands = rest[0], rest[1:]
73	    if command in ("observe", "seen", "export"):
74	        if len(operands) != 1:
75	            _usage()
76	    elif command in ("stats", "restore", "observe-batch", "observe-events"):
77	        if operands:
78	            _usage()
79	    else:
80	        _usage()
81	    return state, command, operands
82	
83	
84	def _open_window(state):
85	    """Load the persisted window, or start an empty one with the defaults.
86	
87	    A missing data file means a fresh window (only possible for the first
88	    observe); every other read failure is corruption and exits 1.
89	    """
90	    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
91	    span, capacity = DEFAULT_SPAN, DEFAULT_CAPACITY
92	    if os.path.exists(path):
93	        try:
94	            span, capacity = read_settings(path)
95	        except ValueError as exc:
96	            _corrupt(str(exc))
97	    try:
98	        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
99	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
100	        _corrupt(str(exc))
101	    if os.path.exists(path):
102	        try:
103	            window.load()
104	        except FileNotFoundError:
105	            pass  # another process removed it between the checks above
106	        except ValueError as exc:
107	            _corrupt(str(exc))
108	    return window
109	
110	
111	def _run_export(state, seq):
112	    """Write the self-checking document of commit ``seq`` to stdout.
113	
114	    Pure read: takes no lock, creates neither the directory nor a state file
115	    and never changes the current state.  A missing/corrupt state file, a
116	    non-positive or unknown commit number is reported as corruption (exit 1)
117	    with an empty stdout.
118	    """
119	    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
120	    try:
121	        span, capacity = read_settings(path)
122	    except FileNotFoundError:
123	        _corrupt("state file is missing")
124	    except ValueError as exc:
125	        _corrupt(str(exc))
126	    try:
127	        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
128	        document = window.export(seq)
129	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
130	        _corrupt(str(exc))
131	    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(document, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
132	
133	
134	def _run_observe_batch(state):
135	    """Atomically observe one JSON array of strings read from stdin.
136	
137	    The whole input -- JSON syntax, list type, element types -- is validated
138	    and an empty result returned before any filesystem call, so an invalid
139	    input creates no directory and leaves an existing state byte for byte
140	    unchanged.  On success stdout holds one compact line of booleans aligned
141	    with the input.  Any failure exits 1 with one ``batch failed`` line on
142	    stderr and an empty stdout.
143	    """
144	    raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
145	    try:
146	        keys = json.loads(raw)
147	    except ValueError as exc:
148	        # Covers an empty input, malformed JSON and trailing junk.
149	        _batch_failed(f"input is not one JSON array: {exc}")
150	    if not isinstance(keys, list) or not all(isinstance(key, str) for key in keys):
151	        _batch_failed("input is not a JSON array of strings")
152	    if not keys:
153	        sys.stdout.write("[]\n")
154	        return
155	    # Open with the persisted settings so a settings mismatch cannot arise;
156	    # every failure (including creating the directory or reading the data
157	    # file) is a batch failure, never the generic corruption text.
158	    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
159	    span, capacity = DEFAULT_SPAN, DEFAULT_CAPACITY
160	    try:
161	        if os.path.exists(path):
162	            span, capacity = read_settings(path)
163	        os.makedirs(state, exist_ok=True)
164	        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
165	        hits = window.observe_many(keys)  # one locked, durable transaction
166	    except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
167	        _batch_failed(str(exc))
168	    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(hits, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
169	
170	
171	def _run_observe_events(state):
172	    """Atomically process one event-time batch read from stdin.
173	
174	    The input is exactly one JSON object holding an ``events`` list and a
175	    ``watermark``; extra fields are ignored.  Input types and ranges are
176	    validated before any filesystem call, so an invalid input creates no
177	    directory and leaves an existing state byte for byte unchanged.  On
178	    success stdout holds one compact JSON line of per-item results.  Any
179	    failure exits 1 with one ``event batch failed`` line on stderr and an
180	    empty stdout.
181	    """
182	    raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
183	    try:
184	        document = json.loads(raw)
185	    except ValueError as exc:
186	        # Covers an empty input, malformed JSON and trailing junk.
187	        _event_batch_failed(f"input is not one JSON object: {exc}")
188	    if not isinstance(document, dict) or "events" not in document \
189	            or "watermark" not in document:
190	        _event_batch_failed("input must be one JSON object with events and watermark")
191	    events = document["events"]
192	    watermark = document["watermark"]
193	    if not isinstance(events, list):
194	        _event_batch_failed("events must be a JSON array")
195	    if not isinstance(watermark, (int, float)) or isinstance(watermark, bool):
196	        _event_batch_failed("watermark must be an int or float")
197	    if not math.isfinite(watermark) or watermark < 0:
198	        _event_batch_failed("watermark must be finite and non-negative")
199	    prepared = []
200	    for event in events:
201	        if not isinstance(event, dict) or "key" not in event \
202	                or "timestamp" not in event:
203	            _event_batch_failed("each event must be an object with key and timestamp")
204	        key = event["key"]
205	        timestamp = event["timestamp"]
206	        if not isinstance(key, str):
207	            _event_batch_failed("event key must be a string")
208	        if not isinstance(timestamp, (int, float)) or isinstance(timestamp, bool):
209	            _event_batch_failed("event timestamp must be an int or float")
210	        if not math.isfinite(timestamp) or timestamp < 0:
211	            _event_batch_failed("event timestamp must be finite and non-negative")
212	        if timestamp > watermark:
213	            _event_batch_failed("event timestamp is later than the watermark")
214	        prepared.append({"key": key, "timestamp": timestamp})
215	    # Open with the persisted settings so a settings mismatch cannot arise;
216	    # the method itself creates the directory only when the batch actually
217	    # has to commit.  Every failure (creating the directory, reading the
218	    # data file) is an event batch failure, never the generic corruption text.
219	    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
220	    span, capacity = DEFAULT_SPAN, DEFAULT_CAPACITY
221	    try:
222	        if os.path.exists(path):
223	            span, capacity = read_settings(path)
224	        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
225	        kinds = window.observe_events(prepared, watermark)
226	    except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
227	        _event_batch_failed(str(exc))
228	    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(kinds, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
229	
230	
231	def _run_restore(state):
232	    """Reset the state atomically from exactly one JSON object on stdin.
233	
234	    The whole document -- JSON type, fields and checksum -- is validated
235	    before any filesystem call, so an invalid input creates no directory and
236	    modifies no state file.  A valid document replaces a missing, healthy or
237	    corrupt old state, after which the same compact JSON a ``stats`` call
238	    prints describes the restored window.
239	    """
240	    raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
241	    try:
242	        document = json.loads(raw)
243	    except ValueError as exc:
244	        # Covers malformed JSON, an empty input and trailing non-whitespace.
245	        _restore_failed(f"input is not one JSON object: {exc}")
246	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
247	        _restore_failed("input is not a JSON object")
248	    try:
249	        # Pure validation only: no directory or file may be touched until the
250	        # document is known to be a valid checkpoint.
251	        _seq, span, capacity, _now, _admitted, _expired, _entries = (
252	            Window._check_restore_document(document)
253	        )
254	        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
255	        window.restore(document)  # one locked, atomic base-file commit
256	    except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
257	        _restore_failed(str(exc))
258	    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(window.stats(), separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
259

261	def main(argv=None):
262	    state, command, operands = _parse(list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv))
263	    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
264	    if command == "observe":
265	        os.makedirs(state, exist_ok=True)
266	        window = _open_window(state)
267	        result = window.observe(operands[0])  # one locked, durable transaction
268	        print(json.dumps(result))
269	    elif command == "seen":
270	        # Pure read: never create the directory, never touch the data file.
271	        if not os.path.exists(path):
272	            print(json.dumps(False))
273	            return 0
274	        window = _open_window(state)
275	        print(json.dumps(window.seen(operands[0])))
276	    elif command == "export":
277	        token = operands[0]
278	        if not _DECIMAL_INT.match(token):
279	            _usage()
280	        _run_export(state, int(token))
281	    elif command == "restore":
282	        _run_restore(state)
283	    elif command == "observe-batch":
284	        _run_observe_batch(state)
285	    elif command == "observe-events":
286	        _run_observe_events(state)
287	    else:
288	        # Pure read: never create the directory, never touch the data file.
289	        if not os.path.exists(path):
290	            print(
291	                json.dumps(
292	                    {
293	                        "span": DEFAULT_SPAN,
294	                        "capacity": DEFAULT_CAPACITY,
295	                        "retained": 0,
296	                        "admitted": 0,
297	                        "expired": 0,
298	                    },
299	                    separators=(",", ":"),
300	                )
301	            )

"""Command line entry point: python3 -m dedupe_window --state <dir> <command>."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import os
import re
import sys

from .window import Window, read_settings

DEFAULT_SPAN = 60
DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 1024

USAGE = (
    "usage: python3 -m dedupe_window --state <dir> "
    "{observe <key> | seen <key> | stats | export <seq> | restore"
    " | observe-batch | observe-events}"
)

# A decimal commit number: one or more decimal digits, optionally signed with
# a leading minus (so non-positive decimals still parse and are rejected as
# out of range rather than as usage errors).
_DECIMAL_INT = re.compile(r"-?[0-9]+\Z")


def _usage():
    print(USAGE, file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(2)


def _corrupt(reason):
    print(f"state file is corrupt: {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(1)


def _restore_failed(reason):
    print(f"restore failed: {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(1)


def _batch_failed(reason):
    print(f"batch failed: {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(1)


def _event_batch_failed(reason):
    print(f"event batch failed: {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(1)


def _parse(argv):
    state = None
    rest = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--state":
            if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                _usage()
            state = argv[i + 1]
            i += 2
        elif arg.startswith("--state="):
            state = arg[len("--state="):]
            i += 1
        else:
            rest.append(arg)
            i += 1
    if not state or len(rest) == 0:
        _usage()
    command, operands = rest[0], rest[1:]
    if command in ("observe", "seen", "export"):
        if len(operands) != 1:
            _usage()
    elif command in ("stats", "restore", "observe-batch", "observe-events"):
        if operands:
            _usage()
    else:
        _usage()
    return state, command, operands


def _open_window(state):
    """Load the persisted window, or start an empty one with the defaults.

    A missing data file means a fresh window (only possible for the first
    observe); every other read failure is corruption and exits 1.
    """
    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
    span, capacity = DEFAULT_SPAN, DEFAULT_CAPACITY
    if os.path.exists(path):
        try:
            span, capacity = read_settings(path)
        except ValueError as exc:
            _corrupt(str(exc))
    try:
        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        _corrupt(str(exc))
    if os.path.exists(path):
        try:
            window.load()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass  # another process removed it between the checks above
        except ValueError as exc:
            _corrupt(str(exc))
    return window


def _run_export(state, seq):
    """Write the self-checking document of commit ``seq`` to stdout.

    Pure read: takes no lock, creates neither the directory nor a state file
    and never changes the current state.  A missing/corrupt state file, a
    non-positive or unknown commit number is reported as corruption (exit 1)
    with an empty stdout.
    """
    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
    try:
        span, capacity = read_settings(path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        _corrupt("state file is missing")
    except ValueError as exc:
        _corrupt(str(exc))
    try:
        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
        document = window.export(seq)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        _corrupt(str(exc))
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(document, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")


def _run_observe_batch(state):
    """Atomically observe one JSON array of strings read from stdin.

    The whole input -- JSON syntax, list type, element types -- is validated
    and an empty result returned before any filesystem call, so an invalid
    input creates no directory and leaves an existing state byte for byte
    unchanged.  On success stdout holds one compact line of booleans aligned
    with the input.  Any failure exits 1 with one ``batch failed`` line on
    stderr and an empty stdout.
    """
    raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    try:
        keys = json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError as exc:
        # Covers an empty input, malformed JSON and trailing junk.
        _batch_failed(f"input is not one JSON array: {exc}")
    if not isinstance(keys, list) or not all(isinstance(key, str) for key in keys):
        _batch_failed("input is not a JSON array of strings")
    if not keys:
        sys.stdout.write("[]\n")
        return
    # Open with the persisted settings so a settings mismatch cannot arise;
    # every failure (including creating the directory or reading the data
    # file) is a batch failure, never the generic corruption text.
    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
    span, capacity = DEFAULT_SPAN, DEFAULT_CAPACITY
    try:
        if os.path.exists(path):
            span, capacity = read_settings(path)
        os.makedirs(state, exist_ok=True)
        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
        hits = window.observe_many(keys)  # one locked, durable transaction
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
        _batch_failed(str(exc))
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(hits, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")


def _run_observe_events(state):
    """Atomically process one event-time batch read from stdin.

    The input is exactly one JSON object holding an ``events`` list and a
    ``watermark``; extra fields are ignored.  Input types and ranges are
    validated before any filesystem call, so an invalid input creates no
    directory and leaves an existing state byte for byte unchanged.  On
    success stdout holds one compact JSON line of per-item results.  Any
    failure exits 1 with one ``event batch failed`` line on stderr and an
    empty stdout.
    """
    raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    try:
        document = json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError as exc:
        # Covers an empty input, malformed JSON and trailing junk.
        _event_batch_failed(f"input is not one JSON object: {exc}")
    if not isinstance(document, dict) or "events" not in document \
            or "watermark" not in document:
        _event_batch_failed("input must be one JSON object with events and watermark")
    events = document["events"]
    watermark = document["watermark"]
    if not isinstance(events, list):
        _event_batch_failed("events must be a JSON array")
    if not isinstance(watermark, (int, float)) or isinstance(watermark, bool):
        _event_batch_failed("watermark must be an int or float")
    if not math.isfinite(watermark) or watermark < 0:
        _event_batch_failed("watermark must be finite and non-negative")
    prepared = []
    for event in events:
        if not isinstance(event, dict) or "key" not in event \
                or "timestamp" not in event:
            _event_batch_failed("each event must be an object with key and timestamp")
        key = event["key"]
        timestamp = event["timestamp"]
        if not isinstance(key, str):
            _event_batch_failed("event key must be a string")
        if not isinstance(timestamp, (int, float)) or isinstance(timestamp, bool):
            _event_batch_failed("event timestamp must be an int or float")
        if not math.isfinite(timestamp) or timestamp < 0:
            _event_batch_failed("event timestamp must be finite and non-negative")
        if timestamp > watermark:
            _event_batch_failed("event timestamp is later than the watermark")
        prepared.append({"key": key, "timestamp": timestamp})
    # Open with the persisted settings so a settings mismatch cannot arise;
    # the method itself creates the directory only when the batch actually
    # has to commit.  Every failure (creating the directory, reading the
    # data file) is an event batch failure, never the generic corruption text.
    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
    span, capacity = DEFAULT_SPAN, DEFAULT_CAPACITY
    try:
        if os.path.exists(path):
            span, capacity = read_settings(path)
        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
        kinds = window.observe_events(prepared, watermark)
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
        _event_batch_failed(str(exc))
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(kinds, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")


def _run_restore(state):
    """Reset the state atomically from exactly one JSON object on stdin.

    The whole document -- JSON type, fields and checksum -- is validated
    before any filesystem call, so an invalid input creates no directory and
    modifies no state file.  A valid document replaces a missing, healthy or
    corrupt old state, after which the same compact JSON a ``stats`` call
    prints describes the restored window.
    """
    raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    try:
        document = json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError as exc:
        # Covers malformed JSON, an empty input and trailing non-whitespace.
        _restore_failed(f"input is not one JSON object: {exc}")
    if not isinstance(document, dict):
        _restore_failed("input is not a JSON object")
    try:
        # Pure validation only: no directory or file may be touched until the
        # document is known to be a valid checkpoint.
        _seq, span, capacity, _now, _admitted, _expired, _entries = (
            Window._check_restore_document(document)
        )
        window = Window(state, span, capacity)
        window.restore(document)  # one locked, atomic base-file commit
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
        _restore_failed(str(exc))
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(window.stats(), separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")


def main(argv=None):
    state, command, operands = _parse(list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv))
    path = os.path.join(state, "window.json")
    if command == "observe":
        os.makedirs(state, exist_ok=True)
        window = _open_window(state)
        result = window.observe(operands[0])  # one locked, durable transaction
        print(json.dumps(result))
    elif command == "seen":
        # Pure read: never create the directory, never touch the data file.
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            print(json.dumps(False))
            return 0
        window = _open_window(state)
        print(json.dumps(window.seen(operands[0])))
    elif command == "export":
        token = operands[0]
        if not _DECIMAL_INT.match(token):
            _usage()
        _run_export(state, int(token))
    elif command == "restore":
        _run_restore(state)
    elif command == "observe-batch":
        _run_observe_batch(state)
    elif command == "observe-events":
        _run_observe_events(state)
    else:
        # Pure read: never create the directory, never touch the data file.
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            print(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "span": DEFAULT_SPAN,
                        "capacity": DEFAULT_CAPACITY,
                        "retained": 0,
                        "admitted": 0,
                        "expired": 0,
                    },
                    separators=(",", ":"),
                )
            )
            return 0
        window = _open_window(state)
        print(json.dumps(window.stats(), separators=(",", ":")))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	"""Bounded deduplication window.
2	
3	A :class:`Window` remembers the first sighting time of each key currently
4	retained.  Two eviction rules apply:
5	
6	* capacity: admitting a new key while the window is full evicts the oldest
7	  key first;
8	* span: :meth:`Window.advance` drops every key whose first sighting is more
9	  than ``span`` behind the current time.
10	
11	Persistence is crash safe and versioned.  The state directory holds exactly
12	one data file, ``window.json``, in a log-structured format: a checksummed
13	base snapshot followed by checksummed records, one per line, chained by
14	sequence number and the previous record's checksum.  Most records are small
15	delta segments, one per committed mutation, so the bytes hitting disk stay
16	proportional to the change instead of mirroring the whole retained state
17	every time.  Periodically a compaction appends an *anchor*: a full snapshot
18	of one commit.  Unlike a rewrite, appending an anchor leaves every earlier
19	record in place, so each commit keeps the number it arrived with and stays
20	locatable: an export returns the same document whether it runs before or
21	after a compaction.  Anchors also bound how far a reader replays.
22	
23	A mutation commits by appending its record in place and fsyncing.  A crash
24	therefore either leaves the last committed state fully recoverable -- an
25	interrupted append only tears the uncommitted tail, which readers ignore and
26	the next writer truncates -- or produces a deterministic error from
27	``load``; a half-restored state is never returned.  A truncated file, a bad
28	checksum or any other tampering raises ``ValueError``; a missing data file
29	raises ``FileNotFoundError``.
30	
31	Documents carry a version number.  The current format is version 3;
32	version 1 documents (a single whole-state JSON object) and version 2
33	documents (a base plus deltas whose compaction rewrote history away) are
34	still read, upgraded in memory and rewritten in the current format on the
35	next commit.  A document without a version, with an unknown version, or
36	left in a half-migrated shape raises ``ValueError``.
37	
38	Read calls never take the lock.  ``keys``, ``seen``, ``stats`` and
39	``export`` open the data file independently of any writer, so a commit or a
40	compaction in progress neither blocks them nor leaks a half-written state:
41	a reader always observes one whole committed prefix and reports exactly
42	that commit -- its key order, counts and current time together, never a
43	mix of an old and a new commit.  Only mutating operations take the advisory
44	``flock``, held on a file descriptor opened on the state directory itself,
45	so no lock file is ever left behind and the kernel releases the lock if a
46	process dies while holding it.  Mutations are linearizable: each runs as
47	lock -> reload -> mutate -> atomic commit, equivalent to some serial
48	execution in arrival order.  Local deployment only; no networking.
49	"""

339	        if first < 0 or first > new_now:
340	            raise ValueError("state file segment holds a sighting outside the timeline")
341	        if new_now - first > span:
342	            raise ValueError("state file segment holds a key older than the span")
343	        if first < max_first:
344	            raise ValueError("state file segment keys are not ordered by first sighting")
345	        adds.append([key, first])
346	    if len(drops) > len(entries) or [key for key, _ in entries[:len(drops)]] != drops:
347	        raise ValueError("state file segment evictions do not match the key order")
348	    if op == "admit":
349	        if new_admitted != admitted + len(adds) or new_expired != expired:
350	            raise ValueError("state file segment counts are inconsistent")
351	    else:
352	        if adds or new_admitted != admitted or new_expired != expired + len(drops):
353	            raise ValueError("state file segment counts are inconsistent")
354	    if drops:
355	        del entries[:len(drops)]
356	        for key in drops:
357	            index.discard(key)
358	    for key, first in adds:
359	        entries.append([key, first])
360	        index.add(key)
361	        max_first = first
362	    if len(entries) > capacity:
363	        raise ValueError("state file holds more keys than the capacity allows")
364	    return new_now, new_admitted, new_expired, seg_seq, document["checksum"], max_first

367	def _parse_v2_log(text):
368	    """Parse a log-structured version 2 file: base line plus delta lines.
369	
370	    Only the final line may be torn (an interrupted append); it is ignored
371	    and its offset recorded so the next writer can truncate it.
372	    """
373	    lines = text.split("\n")
374	    if lines and lines[-1] == "":
375	        lines.pop()
376	    if not lines:
377	        raise ValueError("state file is not valid JSON: the file is empty")
378	    try:
379	        base_doc = json.loads(lines[0])
380	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
381	        raise ValueError(f"state file is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
382	    if not isinstance(base_doc, dict):
383	        raise ValueError("state file must contain a JSON object")
384	    if _version_of(base_doc) != 2:
385	        raise ValueError("state file has an unsupported version")
386	    _, seq, span, capacity, now, admitted, expired, entries = _parse_v2_base(base_doc)
387	    tip = base_doc["checksum"]
388	    index = {key for key, _ in entries}
389	    max_first = entries[-1][1] if entries else 0
390	    base_bytes = len(lines[0].encode("utf-8")) + 1
391	    good_offset = base_bytes
392	    segment_bytes = 0
393	    segment_count = 0
394	    last = len(lines) - 1
395	    for i in range(1, len(lines)):
396	        line_len = len(lines[i].encode("utf-8")) + 1
397	        try:
398	            now, admitted, expired, seq, tip, max_first = _apply_v2_segment(
399	                lines[i],
400	                span=span,
401	                capacity=capacity,
402	                now=now,
403	                admitted=admitted,
404	                expired=expired,
405	                seq=seq,
406	                tip=tip,
407	                entries=entries,
408	                index=index,
409	                max_first=max_first,
410	            )
411	        except ValueError:
412	            if i == last:
413	                break  # torn tail of an interrupted append: ignore it
414	            raise
415	        good_offset += line_len
416	        segment_bytes += line_len
417	        segment_count += 1
418	    return _ParsedState(
419	        version=2,
420	        span=span,
421	        capacity=capacity,
422	        now=now,
423	        admitted=admitted,
424	        expired=expired,
425	        entries=entries,
426	        seq=seq,
427	        tip=tip,
428	        anchor_bytes=base_bytes,
429	        delta_bytes=segment_bytes,
430	        delta_count=segment_count,
431	        good_offset=good_offset,
432	    )

440	def _v3_anchor_info(document, *, allow_base):
441	    """Validate one v3 base/anchor record; return its snapshot info."""
442	    kind = document.get("kind") if isinstance(document, dict) else None
443	    if allow_base:
444	        kinds = ("base", "anchor")
445	    else:
446	        kinds = ("anchor",)
447	    if kind not in kinds:
448	        raise ValueError("state file has an invalid anchor record")
449	    body = _verified_body(document, "state file")

454	        if "prev" in body:
455	            raise ValueError("state file base must not name a predecessor")
456	        prev = None
457	    else:
458	        if seq <= 0:
459	            raise ValueError("state file anchor precedes every commit")
460	        prev = body.get("prev")

462	            raise ValueError("state file anchor has a malformed predecessor")
463	    span, capacity, now, admitted, expired, entries = _validate_snapshot(body)
464	    return {
465	        "kind": kind,
466	        "seq": seq,
467	        "prev": body.get("prev"),
468	        "tip": document["checksum"],
469	        "span": span,
470	        "capacity": capacity,
471	        "now": now,
472	        "admitted": admitted,
473	        "expired": expired,
474	        "entries": entries,

478	def _apply_v3_delta(line, state, index, max_first):
479	    """Validate and replay one v3 delta; mutate ``state`` in place.
480	
481	    The delta is small (evicted keys plus newly admitted ``[key, first]``
482	    pairs); the post-commit state is derived by replay, never stored.
483	    """
484	    try:
485	        document = json.loads(line)
486	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
487	        raise ValueError(f"state file segment is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
488	    if not isinstance(document, dict) or document.get("kind") != "delta":
489	        raise ValueError("state file holds a malformed segment")
490	    body = _verified_body(document, "state file segment")
491	    common = ("seq", "prev", "op")
492	    if any(field not in body for field in common):
493	        raise ValueError("state file holds a malformed segment")
494	    seg_seq = body["seq"]
495	    if not isinstance(seg_seq, int) or isinstance(seg_seq, bool) or seg_seq <= 0:
496	        raise ValueError("state file has an invalid sequence number")
497	    if seg_seq != state["seq"] + 1:
498	        raise ValueError("state file segments are out of order")
499	    if body["prev"] != state["tip"]:
500	        raise ValueError("state file segment chain is broken")
501	    op = body["op"]
502	    if op == "batch":
503	        return _apply_v3_batch_delta(
504	            body, state, index, max_first, document["checksum"]
505	        )
506	    if op == "events":
507	        return _apply_v3_events_delta(
508	            body, state, index, max_first, document["checksum"]
509	        )
510	    fields = ("now", "admitted", "expired", "drop", "add")
511	    if any(field not in body for field in fields):
512	        raise ValueError("state file holds a malformed segment")
513	    if op not in ("admit", "sweep"):
514	        raise ValueError("state file holds a malformed segment")
515	    new_now = body["now"]
516	    if not _is_number(new_now) or new_now < state["now"]:
517	        raise ValueError("state file segment moves time backwards")
518	    new_admitted = body["admitted"]
519	    new_expired = body["expired"]
520	    if not _is_count(new_admitted) or not _is_count(new_expired):
521	        raise ValueError("state file segment has an invalid count")
522	    drops = body["drop"]
523	    if not isinstance(drops, list) or not all(isinstance(key, str) for key in drops):
524	        raise ValueError("state file segment holds malformed evictions")
525	    raw_adds = body["add"]
526	    if not isinstance(raw_adds, list):
527	        raise ValueError("state file segment holds a malformed key entry")
528	    entries = state["entries"]
529	    adds = []
530	    for item in raw_adds:
531	        key, first = _check_entry(item, "state file segment")
532	        if key in index:
533	            raise ValueError("state file segment admits a duplicate key")
534	        if first < 0 or first > new_now:
535	            raise ValueError("state file segment holds a sighting outside the timeline")
536	        if new_now - first > state["span"]:
537	            raise ValueError("state file segment holds a key older than the span")
538	        if first < max_first:
539	            raise ValueError("state file segment keys are not ordered by first sighting")
540	        adds.append([key, first])
541	    if len(drops) > len(entries) or [key for key, _ in entries[:len(drops)]] != drops:
542	        raise ValueError("state file segment evictions do not match the key order")
543	    if op == "admit":
544	        if new_admitted != state["admitted"] + len(adds) or new_expired != state["expired"]:
545	            raise ValueError("state file segment counts are inconsistent")
546	    else:
547	        if adds or new_admitted != state["admitted"] or new_expired != state["expired"] + len(drops):
548	            raise ValueError("state file segment counts are inconsistent")
549	    if drops:
550	        del entries[:len(drops)]
551	        for key in drops:
552	            index.discard(key)
553	    for key, first in adds:
554	        entries.append([key, first])
555	        index.add(key)
556	        max_first = first
557	    if len(entries) > state["capacity"]:
558	        raise ValueError("state file holds more keys than the capacity allows")
559	    state["now"] = new_now
560	    state["admitted"] = new_admitted
561	    state["expired"] = new_expired
562	    state["seq"] = seg_seq
563	    state["tip"] = document["checksum"]
564	    return max_first

567	def _apply_v3_batch_delta(body, state, index, max_first, checksum):
568	    """Validate and replay one v3 atomic batch segment.
569	
570	    A batch records the input keys and the per-item admission results; the
571	    post-commit retained set is fully determined by replaying the inputs
572	    against the pre-batch state, so replay recomputes it and cross-checks
573	    every stored field, including keys admitted and evicted again within the
574	    same commit.
575	    """
576	    fields = ("now", "admitted", "expired", "keys", "hits")
577	    if any(field not in body for field in fields):
578	        raise ValueError("state file holds a malformed segment")
579	    now = body["now"]
580	    if not _is_number(now) or now != state["now"]:
581	        raise ValueError("state file batch segment moves the current time")
582	    new_admitted = body["admitted"]
583	    new_expired = body["expired"]
584	    if not _is_count(new_admitted) or not _is_count(new_expired):
585	        raise ValueError("state file segment has an invalid count")
586	    raw_keys = body["keys"]
587	    raw_hits = body["hits"]
588	    if (
589	        not isinstance(raw_keys, list)
590	        or not raw_keys
591	        or not all(isinstance(key, str) for key in raw_keys)
592	        or not isinstance(raw_hits, list)
593	        or len(raw_hits) != len(raw_keys)
594	        or not all(isinstance(hit, bool) for hit in raw_hits)
595	    ):
596	        raise ValueError("state file batch segment is malformed")
597	    simulated = [list(pair) for pair in state["entries"]]
598	    simulated_index = set(index)
599	    expected_hits = []
600	    capacity = state["capacity"]
601	    for key in raw_keys:
602	        if key in simulated_index:
603	            expected_hits.append(False)
604	            continue
605	        expected_hits.append(True)
606	        while len(simulated) >= capacity:
607	            oldest, _ = simulated.pop(0)
608	            simulated_index.discard(oldest)
609	        simulated.append([key, now])
610	        simulated_index.add(key)
611	    if raw_hits != expected_hits:
612	        raise ValueError("state file batch segment results are inconsistent")
613	    admitted_count = sum(1 for hit in expected_hits if hit)
614	    if new_admitted != state["admitted"] + admitted_count:
615	        raise ValueError("state file segment counts are inconsistent")
616	    if new_expired != state["expired"]:
617	        # Capacity eviction inside a batch is never an expiry.
618	        raise ValueError("state file segment counts are inconsistent")
619	    if len(simulated) > capacity:
620	        raise ValueError("state file holds more keys than the capacity allows")
621	    state["entries"] = simulated
622	    index.clear()
623	    index.update(simulated_index)
624	    state["admitted"] = new_admitted
625	    state["expired"] = new_expired
626	    state["seq"] = body["seq"]
627	    state["tip"] = checksum
628	    return simulated[-1][1] if simulated else max_first
629	
630	
631	_EVENT_KINDS = ("admitted", "duplicate", "late")
632	
633	
634	def _insert_by_first(entries, pair):
635	    """Insert ``[key, first]`` ordered by first sighting, ties last.
636	
637	    Equal timestamps keep admission order: an earlier entry (retained from a
638	    previous commit or admitted earlier in this batch) stays ahead of a new
639	    one.
640	    """
641	    timestamp = pair[1]
642	    lo, hi = 0, len(entries)
643	    while lo < hi:
644	        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
645	        if entries[mid][1] <= timestamp:
646	            lo = mid + 1
647	        else:
648	            hi = mid
649	    entries.insert(lo, pair)
650

652	def _apply_v3_events_delta(body, state, index, max_first, checksum):
653	    """Validate and replay one v3 event-time batch segment.
654	
655	    Like the key batch segment, the segment stores the inputs (each event's
656	    key and timestamp) and the per-item result kinds; replay advances the
657	    watermark, expires the span prefix and recomputes every classification,
658	    including a key expired or capacity-evicted and readmitted within the
659	    same commit.
660	    """
661	    fields = ("now", "admitted", "expired", "wmark", "events", "kinds")
662	    if any(field not in body for field in fields):
663	        raise ValueError("state file holds a malformed segment")
664	    pre_now = state["now"]
665	    wmark = body["wmark"]
666	    if not _is_finite_time(wmark) or wmark != pre_now:
667	        raise ValueError("state file events segment moves the previous watermark")
668	    new_now = body["now"]
669	    if not _is_finite_time(new_now) or new_now < pre_now:
670	        raise ValueError("state file segment moves time backwards")
671	    new_admitted = body["admitted"]
672	    new_expired = body["expired"]
673	    if not _is_count(new_admitted) or not _is_count(new_expired):
674	        raise ValueError("state file segment has an invalid count")
675	    raw_events = body["events"]
676	    raw_kinds = body["kinds"]
677	    if (
678	        not isinstance(raw_events, list)
679	        or not isinstance(raw_kinds, list)
680	        or len(raw_kinds) != len(raw_events)
681	        or not all(isinstance(kind, str) and kind in _EVENT_KINDS
682	                   for kind in raw_kinds)
683	    ):
684	        raise ValueError("state file events segment is malformed")
685	    events = []
686	    for item in raw_events:
687	        key, timestamp = _check_entry(item, "state file segment")
688	        if not _is_finite_time(timestamp) or timestamp > new_now:
689	            raise ValueError("state file segment holds an event outside the timeline")
690	        events.append((key, timestamp))
691	
692	    span = state["span"]
693	    capacity = state["capacity"]
694	    simulated = [list(pair) for pair in state["entries"]]
695	    simulated_index = set(index)
696	    expiry_count = 0
697	    while simulated and new_now - simulated[0][1] > span:
698	        oldest, _ = simulated.pop(0)
699	        simulated_index.discard(oldest)
700	        expiry_count += 1
701	    expected_kinds = []
702	    admitted_count = 0
703	    for key, timestamp in events:
704	        if new_now - timestamp > span:
705	            expected_kinds.append("late")
706	            continue
707	        if key in simulated_index:
708	            expected_kinds.append("duplicate")
709	            continue
710	        expected_kinds.append("admitted")
711	        admitted_count += 1
712	        while len(simulated) >= capacity:
713	            oldest, _ = simulated.pop(0)
714	            simulated_index.discard(oldest)
715	        pair = [key, timestamp]
716	        _insert_by_first(simulated, pair)
717	        simulated_index.add(key)
718	    if raw_kinds != expected_kinds:
719	        raise ValueError("state file events segment results are inconsistent")
720	    if new_admitted != state["admitted"] + admitted_count:
721	        raise ValueError("state file segment counts are inconsistent")
722	    if new_expired != state["expired"] + expiry_count:
723	        raise ValueError("state file segment counts are inconsistent")
724	    if len(simulated) > capacity:
725	        raise ValueError("state file holds more keys than the capacity allows")
726	    state["entries"] = simulated
727	    index.clear()
728	    index.update(simulated_index)
729	    state["now"] = new_now
730	    state["admitted"] = new_admitted
731	    state["expired"] = new_expired
732	    state["seq"] = body["seq"]
733	    state["tip"] = checksum
734	    return simulated[-1][1] if simulated else max_first

757	def _parse_v3(text):
758	    """Parse a version 3 log from its base snapshot.
759	
760	    Every record is checksum-verified and the prev/seq chain is checked
761	    against the record immediately before it, so a tampered record is caught
762	    even when an anchor follows it.  Only the final line may be torn (an
763	    interrupted append); it is ignored.
764	    """
765	    lines = _split_lines(text)
766	    if not lines:
767	        raise ValueError("state file is not valid JSON: the file is empty")
768	    last = len(lines) - 1
769	
770	    def load_line(i):
771	        try:
772	            return json.loads(lines[i])
773	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
774	            raise ValueError(f"state file is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
775	
776	    # The first record is always the base snapshot (commit 0).
777	    base_doc = load_line(0)
778	    if not isinstance(base_doc, dict):
779	        raise ValueError("state file must contain a JSON object")
780	    base_info = _v3_anchor_info(base_doc, allow_base=True)
781	    if base_info["kind"] != "base":
782	        raise ValueError("state file has an invalid base snapshot")
783	
784	    state = _state_from_anchor(base_info)
785	    index = {key for key, _ in state["entries"]}
786	    max_first = state["entries"][-1][1] if state["entries"] else 0
787	    base_len = len(lines[0].encode("utf-8")) + 1
788	    good_offset = base_len
789	    delta_bytes = 0
790	    delta_count = 0
791	    anchor_len = base_len
792	    prev_tip = base_info["tip"]
793	    prev_seq = base_info["seq"]
794	
795	    for i in range(1, len(lines)):
796	        line_len = len(lines[i].encode("utf-8")) + 1
797	        torn = i == last
798	        try:
799	            document = load_line(i)
800	            if not isinstance(document, dict):
801	                raise ValueError("state file must contain a JSON object")
802	            kind = document.get("kind")
803	            if kind == "anchor":
804	                info = _v3_anchor_info(document, allow_base=False)
805	                if info["prev"] != prev_tip or info["seq"] != prev_seq + 1:
806	                    raise ValueError("state file anchor chain is broken")
807	                if info["span"] != state["span"] or info["capacity"] != state["capacity"]:
808	                    raise ValueError("state file anchor changes the settings")
809	                # Counts are monotone across commits; the anchor's own
810	                # checksum already binds its snapshot to its bytes.
811	                if info["admitted"] < state["admitted"] or info["expired"] < state["expired"]:
812	                    raise ValueError("state file anchor counts are inconsistent")
813	            elif kind == "delta":
814	                max_first = _apply_v3_delta(lines[i], state, index, max_first)
815	            else:
816	                raise ValueError("state file holds a malformed record")
817	        except ValueError:
818	            if torn:
819	                break  # torn tail of an interrupted append: ignore it
820	            raise
821	        if kind == "anchor":
822	            state = _state_from_anchor(info)
823	            index = {key for key, _ in state["entries"]}
824	            max_first = state["entries"][-1][1] if state["entries"] else 0
825	            anchor_len = line_len
826	            delta_bytes = 0
827	            delta_count = 0
828	        else:
829	            delta_bytes += line_len
830	            delta_count += 1
831	        prev_tip = state["tip"]
832	        prev_seq = state["seq"]
833	        good_offset += line_len
834	
835	    return _ParsedState(
836	        version=3,
837	        span=state["span"],
838	        capacity=state["capacity"],
839	        now=state["now"],
840	        admitted=state["admitted"],
841	        expired=state["expired"],
842	        entries=state["entries"],
843	        seq=state["seq"],
844	        tip=state["tip"],
845	        anchor_bytes=anchor_len,
846	        delta_bytes=delta_bytes,
847	        delta_count=delta_count,
848	        good_offset=good_offset,
849	    )

881	def _parse_state_file(path):
882	    """Read, verify and replay the state file at ``path``.
883	
884	    Raises FileNotFoundError when the file is absent and ValueError for
885	    every form of corruption: bad formatting, a missing or unknown version,
886	    a missing or mismatched checksum, a broken chain or state that violates
887	    the window invariants.  A torn final record left by a crashed writer is
888	    not corruption; it is ignored.
889	
890	    The read takes no lock.  It observes one whole file content: a commit
891	    appended concurrently can only tear the final line (ignored), and a
892	    compaction or restore that replaces the file via ``os.replace`` lands as
893	    either the old or the new complete file -- never a mixture.
894	    """
895	    try:
896	        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
897	            raw = fh.read()
898	    except FileNotFoundError:
899	        raise
900	    except OSError as exc:
901	        raise ValueError(f"state file cannot be read: {exc}") from exc
902	    text = _decode(raw)
903	    try:
904	        document = json.loads(text)
905	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
906	        document = None
907	    if document is not None:
908	        # A single JSON object: a version 1/2 document, or a v3 file that so
909	        # far holds only its base snapshot.
910	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
911	            raise ValueError("state file must contain a JSON object")
912	        version = _version_of(document)
913	        if version == 1:
